task.description: WF-02 step 8, item 1: BA-ANALYST (role file .claude/agents/ba-analyst.md) writes the acceptance scenarios for REQ-113 (the visitor status block) in docs/uat/REQ-113.md, in the form of docs/uat/REQ-111.md: one main-path scenario per criterion that a person can see (3 the block on the demo result and on how.html; 4 the lead above «Описать идею» and no grey line; 5 «Учтено ответов» and its sentence incl. the «Не знаю» case showing «4 из 5»; 6 the stage marks and the two notes; 7 the language switch; 10 layout and contrast; 12 the reader test) and one per failure path (the demo API does not answer, a 500 on the result request, JavaScript off on how.html, storage that throws, slow network) with the bad conditions of the REQ-111 file. Each scenario names its criteria and has the line 'Browser step (UAT-RUNNER, real Chrome; 1470x784, 390x844, 320x568; light and dark; ru and en): <steps> -> <observable result>', a 'Cells' line, 'Expected' taken from the criterion VERBATIM (anything wider is a remark, AP-117), Evidence and 'If not so' with severity. Languages: ru and en are run; kk is hidden on production (G9) and its texts wait for a native speaker (ISS-0127): kk scenarios are written as 'not run: kk hidden, G9'. Criterion 12's reader test: take its wording from the requirement exactly: write the questions (three per the requirement) for a reader who sees only the page (no repository, no explanation), with the expected answers and the scoring rule (Part A for the reader, Part B the key, not for the reader) as R-01 of the REQ-111 file does. Stand: ORCH will start the app from a fresh clone and give the address; use the placeholder <APP>. No scenario spends the owner's limit (no real AI run, G2). Criteria with no person-visible scenario (tests, counts, CI) are listed with their checkers. Facts to check first (quality-bar section 6): the criteria in docs/requirements.yaml, the look, the built texts (app/public/shared/i18n/texts.js and how.html of the working tree). Do NOT run npm run check, the app test scripts or e2e tests on this PC (the owner's rule); you only write a document; allowed: cd tools && npm run -s handoffs-check and traces. English (decisions/0080), page texts in Russian and English. No commit/push. Fill result (summary, scenario list with the criteria each covers, criteria without a scenario); status stays PENDING; ORCH closes.

issues.text: V-20 (criterion 8, the public set) goes beyond the list in the task (3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 10, 12): criterion 8 is visible to a person on the public stand, and the role rule asks a scenario for every such criterion. It needs <APP-PUBLIC>, as REQ-111 L-34; if ORCH does not start that stand the scenario is 'not run: no stand'. ORCH may drop it; then criterion 8 stays with the tests (LD-9, PB-*) and the post-deploy record.

Criteria 3 and 6 name the failure states only through the design (design section 5 rows 4, 5, 6): the criteria do not say that the block stands while the result request fails or is absent when the questionnaire fails. V-13 and V-14 therefore take only the console and CSP rule of criterion 10 and the REQ-111 criterion 12 message as Expected, and put the block's presence in those states as a Remark (not a failure). If the owner wants those states to be a criterion, it goes through WF-01.

R-01 Part A adds one framing line to the three questions ('take the demo survey to its result, then open Как это работает'), because criterion 12 says the reader takes the survey and opens how.html; the three questions are the criterion's words. The Part B key is for BA-ANALYST and the scorer only; ORCH must copy only Part A to the reader.

Unclear point left as a scoring decision, not a guess in the requirement: question 3 of the reader test has two halves (cannot describe an idea now; finished products not handed out). The scoring rule says both halves must be named. An answer that says 'not found' is wrong for all three questions because the block says each fact in words.
